newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslem refugees return home in Croat territory.
newsitem.headline: Moslem refugees return home in Croat territory.

text.p: Moslem refugees have been allowed to return home and move around freely for the first time in a western Bosnian town controlled by hardline Croat nationalists, the U.N. said on Friday.

In a rare piece of good news about refugees seeking to go home in divided postwar Bosnia, 74 Moslems have re-entered the town of Stolac to rebuild their houses, a spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees said.
Local ethnic nationalist authorities have resisted international efforts to resettle minority inhabitants in much of Bosnia but especially in the separatist Serb republic.

Stolac was one of four towns in Bosnia's troubled Moslem- Croat federation designated for pilot projects to repatriate refugees. Three towns have generally cooperated, but until recently Croat authorities in Stolac had allowed Moslems back in only briefly before ordering them out.

"In Stolac we have had a bit of a breakthrough. After a two-month break, 74 Moslems were allowed to go into Stolac again to repair their homes," UNHCR spokesman Kris Janowski told reporters in Sarajevo.
"What is so significant about this visit yesterday is that the Moslems were not confined to one street. They could actually wander around the whole town which they never have been before," he said.
"We hope Stolac, which had been the last town to be totally blocked, will make the implementation of the pilot projects complete."

Stolac is situated in the Herzegovina region of southwest Bosnia where separatist Croat forces in Bosnia's war declared a breakaway state in 1993 and have failed to abolish it in defiance of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty.
